skill.name: normalize
skill.description: Normalize an existing interface so it follows the project design system, component patterns, and accessibility standards.
skill.summary: Align UI features with established design system standards and reusable components.
skill.author: pbakaus

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 49 refers to UI spacing and layout grid systems in a design-system checklist. It does not request host, network, or environment reconnaissance.

content.user_title: Normalize Interfaces to Your Design System
content.value_statement: Inconsistent interface details make products harder to maintain and use. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through structured UI normalization against existing design standards.
actual_capabilities: Find design system documentation, component libraries, and style guides in a project.
Compare a feature against established typography, color, spacing, layout, and component patterns.
Plan interface changes that replace one-off styles with design tokens and reusable components.
Check responsive behavior, focus states, labels, and contrast against project standards.
Guide cleanup of obsolete styles, duplicated components, and unused UI code after normalization.
limitations: It depends on existing design system context or a separate discovery step.
It does not create a complete design system from nothing.
It cannot guarantee visual approval without human review or screenshots.
It should not override product requirements that intentionally differ from existing patterns.

use_cases.title: Unify a New Feature
use_cases.description: Align a recently built page with shared components, tokens, and interaction patterns before release.

use_cases.title: Prepare Design Debt Work
use_cases.description: Identify inconsistent UI decisions and create a focused plan for reducing one-off implementation debt.

use_cases.title: Review Product Consistency
use_cases.description: Check whether a product area follows established accessibility, responsive, and layout conventions.

prompt_templates.title: Normalize a Page
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one known route.
prompt_templates.prompt: Normalize the settings page so it follows our design system. First find the relevant design guidance, then propose and apply focused UI changes.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Before Editing
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request when the team wants a plan first.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the billing flow against our design system. List the main inconsistencies by typography, color, spacing, components, responsive behavior, and accessibility before editing.

prompt_templates.title: Replace One-Off UI
prompt_templates.prompt: Find custom UI in the dashboard summary area that should use existing shared components. Replace it with design system equivalents where appropriate.

prompt_templates.title: Normalize and Verify
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for a complete implementation pass.
prompt_templates.prompt: Normalize the account onboarding flow end to end. Use repository design guidance, update inconsistent UI, remove obsolete styles, and run the relevant checks.

output_examples.output: The dashboard now uses shared card, table, and button patterns. Spacing uses project tokens, empty states match existing language, and focus styles remain visible.

output_examples.input: Review this profile page for design system drift.
output: Typography differs from the profile settings pattern.
Primary actions use a custom color instead of the action token.
The mobile layout does not follow the standard stacked form pattern.

output_examples.input: Make the checkout step match the rest of the app.
output_examples.output: The checkout step now follows the shared form layout, uses standard error messaging, and keeps the responsive action bar consistent with other flows.

best_practices: Gather design system context before making visual changes.
Prefer shared components and tokens over new local styles.
Verify accessibility, responsive behavior, and regression checks after edits.
anti_patterns: Do not invent new components when suitable shared components already exist.
Do not hard-code colors, spacing, or typography that should come from tokens.
Do not chase visual polish while ignoring usability or accessibility differences.

faq.question: What does this skill normalize?
faq.answer: It normalizes interface details such as typography, color, spacing, layout, components, motion, responsive behavior, and accessibility.

faq.question: Does it need an existing design system?
faq.answer: Yes. It works best when the repository has documented patterns, shared components, tokens, or prior product screens to follow.

faq.question: Can it create new shared components?
faq.answer: It can recommend or move reusable components when needed, but it first looks for existing design system equivalents.

faq.question: Does it only change visual styling?
faq.answer: No. It also considers usability, information hierarchy, responsive behavior, interaction patterns, and accessibility.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: How should teams review its changes?
faq.answer: Teams should review screenshots or previews, confirm design intent, and run the repository lint, type, and test checks.
